item.title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin Achieves 10× Agentic Throughput Per Kilowatt in MLPerf Endpoints v1.0
item.description:
NVIDIA Vera Rubin Achieves 10× Agentic Throughput Per Kilowatt in MLPerf Endpoints v1.0

NVIDIA released provisional results for its Vera Rubin NVL72 platform in the MLPerf Endpoints v1.0 benchmark, showing more than 10× the agentic throughput per kilowatt compared to the verified GB300 NVL72 while maintaining a minimum end‑to‑end interactivity of 50 tokens per second per user.

🔍 Overview

  • Agentic workloads are demanding more from inference systems.
  • AI agents carry growing conversation histories across turns and generate a mix of reasoning, tool calls, and responses.
  • Inference systems must support users at scale while remaining responsive.
  • The MLPerf Endpoints v1.0 dataset captures coding trajectories that accumulate history over many turns and enterprise workflows that reuse shared instructions, tool definitions, and business rules.

🧩 How It Works

  • The benchmark evaluates serving capacity and responsiveness using coding and enterprise workflows through API endpoints.
  • During performance runs, generated tool calls and workflow intent are checked against reference values.
  • Separate SWE‑bench Verified evaluations assess end‑to‑end task‑solving capability.
  • These checks evaluate whether faster serving preserves model quality.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Vera Rubin NVL72 (32 accelerators)
    • Run 9: concurrency = 1,024 queries
    • TTFT P90 = 4,673.9 ms
    • System TPS = 41,414.2 tokens/sec
    • E2E average interactivity = 50.4 tokens/sec per user
    • Operating power = 100.89 kW
  • GB300 NVL72 (48 accelerators)
    • Run 6: concurrency = 48 queries
    • TTFT P90 = 2,305.1 ms
    • System TPS = 2,210.4 tokens/sec
    • E2E average interactivity = 56.2 tokens/sec per user
    • Operating power = 60 kW

📊 Performance Results for Model Variants

  • Kimi K3
    • Vera Rubin: run 9, 1,024 queries, 41,414.2 TPS, 50.4 interactivity, 100.89 kW
    • GB300: run 6, 48 queries, 2,210.4 TPS, 56.2 interactivity, 60 kW
  • DeepSeek‑V4.1‑Flash
    • Vera Rubin: run 6, 1,408 queries, 272,711.7 TPS, 294.49 interactivity, 75.67 kW
    • GB300: run 1, 16 queries, 3,054.0 TPS, 288.65 interactivity, 7.50 kW
  • Qwen3.6‑35B‑A3B
    • Vera Rubin: run 8, 320 queries, 47,785.5 TPS, 411.9 interactivity, 12.61 kW
    • GB300: run 2, 36 queries, 5,960.4 TPS, 531.6 interactivity, 7.50 kW

📈 Tradeoff Curve

  • Figure 2 shows the tradeoff between throughput per provisioned kilowatt and E2E interactivity across at least seven concurrency levels per curve.
  • The curves illustrate how much throughput each system delivers at a given responsiveness requirement.

🔬 Verification Status

  • GB300 results are verified by the MLCommons Association.
  • Vera Rubin results are provisional.
  • Pending MLCommons Association verification, results may change.

#MLPerf #NVIDIA #Inference #AgenticWorkloads #Throughput

Source: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Leads Agentic Inference Performance on MLPerf Endpoints v1.0 | NVIDIA Technical Blog

item.title: NVIDIA Vera Rubin Architecture Debuts in MLPerf Training v6.1
item.description:
NVIDIA Vera Rubin Architecture Debuts in MLPerf Training v6.1

NVIDIA’s Vera Rubin architecture has made its debut in MLPerf Training v6.1, showcasing impressive performance and scalability. The new architecture, along with its CUDA software stack, has demonstrated significant advancements in AI training capabilities.

🔍 Overview

  • MLPerf Training v6.1 marks the debut of the NVIDIA Vera Rubin architecture.
  • Vera Rubin NVL72 platform delivered the fastest time to train on six of the seven benchmarks.
  • NVIDIA platforms hold the fastest time to train on every benchmark in v6.1.
  • Vera Rubin successfully completed the entire suite in its inaugural run.

⚙️ Key Details

  • Vera Rubin NVL72 achieved up to 2x more performance than a highly optimized NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 baseline.
  • For the DeepSeek-V3 671B benchmark, NVIDIA demonstrated massive scale on a 10,240-GPU GB300 NVL72 cluster.
  • Vera Rubin maintained above 97% overall efficiency when scaling from 256 to 1,024 GPUs.
  • NVIDIA platforms were the only ones to submit results across all seven benchmarks.

🚀 Availability

  • The Vera Rubin architecture is now available and has been tested in MLPerf Training v6.1.

💡 Why it Matters

  • The performance gains span the entire modeling pipeline, supporting everything from large-scale pretraining to reinforcement learning post-training.
  • The new architecture is designed to handle the most demanding workloads, including the 671-billion-parameter token-dropless Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model.
  • The Vera Rubin platform also proved its flexibility by submitting on two different inference backends: NVIDIA NeMo RL with TensorRT-LLM and with vLLM.
  • The NVIDIA Vera CPU is integral to the architecture, sustaining more than 22,500 concurrent RL environments across 256 CPUs in a single Vera CPU rack.

#NVIDIA #VeraRubin #MLPerf #AITraining #CUDA #DeepLearning

Source: NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 Achieves up to 2x Blackwell Ultra Performance in MLPerf Training v6.1 | NVIDIA Technical Blog

item.title: NVIDIA TensorRT Edge-LLM Performance in MLPerf Inference v6.1 Edge Agentic Benchmark
item.description:
NVIDIA TensorRT Edge-LLM Performance in MLPerf Inference v6.1 Edge Agentic Benchmark

NVIDIA TensorRT Edge-LLM has completed the MLPerf Inference v6.1 Edge Agentic benchmark running the Qwen3.6-27B model on a single NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor Developer Kit.

⚙️ Key details

The system was configured with the following specifications:

  • Hardware: One NVIDIA Jetson AGX Thor Developer Kit
  • Memory: 128 GB of unified memory
  • Power Mode: MAXN
  • Execution Mode: SingleStream
  • Model: Qwen3.6-27B

📊 Performance results

The TensorRT Edge-LLM submission completed the performance workload in 24 minutes and 36 seconds, which is 6.4x faster than the llama.cpp reference submission of 2 hours and 37 minutes.

Metric Value
Output throughput 52.33 tokens per second
Median time to first token 247.12 ms
Median time per output token 14.68 ms
BFCL overall accuracy 87.94%

🧩 How it works

The result was achieved using several optimization techniques:

  • Quantization: The submission used NVFP4 (a 4-bit floating-point format supported by the NVIDIA Blackwell GPU) for weights and activations, including the language-model head, and FP8 for the KV cache. This smaller representation increases available unified memory for application workloads, speculative decoding state, and long context.
  • KV Cache Reuse: TensorRT Edge-LLM identifies reusable prompt prefixes and restores cached attention KV pages. Because Qwen3.6 uses a hybrid model architecture, the runtime also restores partial KV-page state and the recurrent state. In this workload, approximately 96% of prompt tokens were served with hot cache, requiring the prefill of only ~0.5M of the 13.6M total prompt tokens.
  • Tree-based Multi-Token Prediction (MTP): A draft model predicts several future tokens which the target model verifies together in one forward pass. The server configuration utilized:
    • 8 draft steps
    • Top-2 candidates at each drafting depth
    • A 16-node verification tree

🔍 Overview

The MLPerf Edge Agentic benchmark measures OpenAI-compatible model endpoints across two phases:

  • Performance: The workload consists of 20 conversations and 1,007 generated turns. Input length grows to approximately 23.5K tokens.
  • Accuracy: This phase uses Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL) v4 prompts with reasoning off and single-turn only to balance evaluation time and accuracy on edge devices.

#MLPerf #TensorRT #JetsonAGXThor #EdgeAI #LLM

Source: TensorRT Edge-LLM Completes the MLPerf Edge Agentic Benchmark 6.4x Faster on Jetson AGX Thor | NVIDIA Technical Blog
